newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yaohan Japan sheds early gains on Gajoen woes.
newsitem.headline: Yaohan Japan sheds early gains on Gajoen woes.

text.p: Shares in Yaohan Japan Corp shed earlier gains in Tuesday afternoon trade, depressed by news that debt-laden Gajoen Kanko KK had failed to pay promissory notes for a second time, brokers said.
A second failure to pay such notes is regarded in Japanese business practice as effectively a bankruptcy.
As of 0526 GMT, supermarket chain operator Yaohan Japan's shares were down three yen at 408 yen.
"The knee-jerk reaction of some investors when news of this sort appears is to sell shares of companies which are struggling financially," a strategist at a second-tier brokerage said.

Under a restructuring plan unveiled on Monday, Yaohan Japan said it aims to slash its group assets to 170 billion yen by the end of March 1999 from 249.4 billion yen as of the end of March 1996. It also plans to trim group debt subject to interest payments to 90 billion yen from 164.6 billion yen.

In an attempt to calm market worries that Yaohan may be facing problems in meeting fund demand partly from planned redemption of its bonds, company president Mitsumasa Wada said Yaohan would receive necessary help from its main banks.
He said the company would use the banks' financial assistance for daily operations and might seek further help to redeem corporate bonds later this year if necessary.
The restructuring plan initially lifted the shares to 420 yen early in the morning session.
